scope: Metadata-only audit of frozen baseline query annotations. No relabeling, exclusion, rescoring or denominator change.

schema.positive: Top-1 answer must belong to the truth list.
schema.negative: Top-1 answer must not equal row.slug. Frozen negative truth lists are empty. An allowed answer is not a verified identification.

source_references.role: Query selection and saved query fields; positive [place], negative empty truth.
classify uses truth membership and negative forbidden-slug fallback.

definitions.disjoint_positive_pair: Two positive truth sets have empty intersection.
definitions.positive_group_conflict: The intersection of all positive truth sets for one digest is empty. Different but overlapping truth sets alone do not establish a conflict.
definitions.direct_positive_negative_conflict: A positive truth set contains only the slug forbidden by one negative row.
definitions.combined_negative_conflict: All members of a positive truth set are forbidden by negative rows of the same digest.
definitions.joint_compatibility: At least one slug belongs to every positive truth set and to none of the same-digest negative forbidden slugs.
definitions.all_positive_row_pairs_disjoint: Every pair of positive rows has disjoint truth sets. Repeated identical positive labels prevent this property even if the group contains a conflicting pair.

assumptions: Each recorded image_sha256 group is treated as identical input bytes. Source files were not opened or rehashed.
The recognizer returns one deterministic top-1 wine slug for each image byte sequence.
The recognizer does not use query_id, image_path, folder/place slug, labels, truth, row order, or other row-specific metadata.
The same input does not receive different answers through randomness, time-dependent state, or request-specific context.
A positive row is correct when the answer belongs to its full accepted truth list. Truth lists are sets of alternatives, not one mandatory answer per list element.
Each positive query row has equal weight, including repeated rows. The denominator stays 1644.
The bound optimizes each digest independently and ignores recognition difficulty, missing index coverage, and operational errors. It is optimistic.
The bound concerns positive top-1 recall only. It is not a top-5 bound or an accuracy score for negative rows.
deterministic_positive_top1_ceiling.formula: For digest d, m_d = max over answer a of sum over its positive rows i of 1[a in truth_i]. The ceiling numerator is sum_d m_d.
deterministic_positive_top1_ceiling.status: Conditional metadata ceiling. No observed predictions are read or rescored.

notes: All 1644 positive truth lists contain one slug in this frozen baseline. The analysis uses full set membership and does not assume that future truth lists are singleton.
All 584 negative rows have empty truth lists and exclude only their row.slug.

The conflict labels refer to exact saved slug constraints. This audit does not decide whether different slugs are aliases, which annotation is physically correct, or whether catalogue entities should merge.
The result is not permission to edit labels or remove rows. All raw benchmark denominators and metrics remain unchanged.
No source image, live database, inference service, or current index was accessed.
The previously documented q-000483/q-000484 pilot conflict is one of these groups. The q-000152/q-000160 positive/negative pair is compatible.

These are incompatible exact-slug constraints under the same-bytes, same-answer assumption, not established annotation mistakes. The same photo may intentionally represent multiple catalogue identities. No correct label or model-achievable recall is inferred.
